Thirdly, because in this life they are tried by various tribulations, temptations and adversities. Yet she owns herself beautiful, because there are always many virtuous and holy men in her, and all who are truly made members of her are adorned with charity, infused virtues and the gifts of the Holy Ghost. She has the sacraments too, by which she is daily renewed and made beautiful. So: [[1:4|I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, souls, or young maidens and particular Churches, [[1:4|as the tents of Cedar|sicut tabernacula Cedar]]: Cedar was the second son of Ismael[[Gen 25:13||]], and lived with his offspring and household in tents, in the wilderness or desert; and so his tents, though at times unsightly without, being exposed to winds and rains, were within full of riches and cattle. [[1:4|as the curtains of Solomon|sicut pelles Salomonis]] [Latin *pelles*, skins or hides, where the Douay-Rheims has "curtains"]: with which he adorned his house or bridal chamber, or covered the tabernacle of God or its vessels. But Solomon is better understood as Christ, whose skins are the fair garments of his ministers and the ornaments of divine worship, and also the manners and outward bearing, the gait and attire of Christ himself, to which his Bride conforms herself as far as she can. For with these, as with the finest skins, the Church is clothed and adorned. Lastly, by the tents of Cedar may be understood the faithless and the heathen, to whom unbelieving Judea, despising the Church, reckoned her alike.

paras.t: Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim, id est obscura seu denigrata, juxta sensum quo dixi, Nigra sum; quia decoloravit me sol, id est, comparatione sanctitatis, perfectionis ac sapientiæ sponsi mei, qui est Sol sapientiæ atque justitiæ, fuscam me fateor: qui etiam legem tantæ perfectionis contulit mihi, quod a perfecta ejus observatione deficio; sicque legis suæ splendore me fuscam demonstrat. Rursus, Decoloravit me sol, id est, intuitu et amore solis istius, videlicet sponsi, exposui me tribulationibus, persecutionibus ac aspernationibus impiorum, laboribusque diversis ac multis doloribus: propter quos videor decolorata, et quasi relicta a sponso. Sed hæc omnia intus me ornant: idcirco nolite ista in me ita considerare, ut metu sustinendi talia, recedatis a fide et obedientia mea; sed præmia illa æterna pro his momentaneis afflictionibus exhibenda, perpendite, et gaudete in talibus, sicut in Evangelio sponsus hortatur: Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Postremo, per solem hoc loco quidam æstum tribulationis intelligunt.
paras.en: [[1:5|Do not consider me that I am brown|Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim]], that is, dark or blackened, in the sense in which I said, [[1:4|I am black|Nigra sum]]; [[1:5|because the sun hath altered my colour|quia decoloravit me sol]]: that is, I confess myself brown in comparison with the holiness, perfection and wisdom of my Bridegroom, who is the Sun of wisdom and justice; who has also given me a law of such perfection that I fall short of keeping it perfectly; and so by the splendour of his law he shows me to be brown. Again, [[1:5|the sun hath altered my colour|decoloravit me sol]]: that is, for the sake of beholding and loving this Sun, namely the Bridegroom, I have exposed myself to tribulations, persecutions and the contempt of the wicked, to labours of many kinds and many sorrows; because of which I seem discoloured, and as it were forsaken by the Bridegroom. But all these adorn me within; therefore do not so consider these things in me that for fear of suffering the like you draw back from my faith and obedience; but weigh those eternal rewards that are to be given for these momentary afflictions, and rejoice in such things, as the Bridegroom exhorts in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:12|Be glad|Gaudete]] in that hour [[Matt 5:12|and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]] [Denis's "in that hour" is closer to Luke 6:23, "in that day"]. Lastly, some take the sun in this place for the heat of tribulation.

paras.t: Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me. Ecclesia primitiva ex Judæis atque gentilibus fuit collecta, sicque mater Ecclesiæ partim fuit ipsa gentilitas, partim plebs Judæorum. Ipsam autem Ecclesiam primitivam multis annis acerrime impugnaverunt tam infideles ac obstinati Judæi, quam gentiles increduli, prout in Actibus Apostolorum partim describitur, atque in chronicis, historiis et legendis Sanctorum plenius continetur. Judæi autem impugnaverunt eam tam allegationibus Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, quam persecutione reali. Similiter gentiles philosophi, ratione naturali variis modis contra Ecclesiam dimicarunt; reges vero et tyranni fecerunt hoc gladio materiali. Et sicut sponsus prædixit, tradebantur credentes in eum a parentibus, fratribus, cognatis et amicis, et morte afficiebantur ab eis. — Insuper universalis Ecclesia in persona particularium Ecclesiarum, hoc est quæcumque particularis Ecclesia, dicere potest: Filii matris meæ, hoc est hæretici qui ad tempus fuerunt universalis Ecclesiæ filii (de quibus in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes apostolus, Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis), pugnaverunt contra me, quia valde fuerunt infesti Catholicis, potissime Ariani: qui et corporaliter pluribus annis persequebantur et jugulabant fideles. Similiter impii Christiani, schismatici, principesque iniqui et vitiosi prælati pugnant adversus Ecclesiam, justos vexando, pusillos ac subditos scandalizando, injusta prælia suscitando, aut ecclesiasticis non obediendo mandatis. Et certe pia mater Ecclesia, quæ a malignis spiritibus et ab infidelibus populis incessanter gravissime impugnatur, non mediocriter contristatur, dum filios suos, qui se deberent mutuo contra prætactos hostes acerrimos adjuvare, videt contra se matrem ipsorum et contra se invicem decertare.
paras.en: [[1:5|the sons of my mother have fought against me|Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me]]. The early Church was gathered from Jews and Gentiles, and so the mother of the Church was partly the Gentile world itself and partly the Jewish people. And this early Church was most fiercely assailed for many years both by the unbelieving and obstinate Jews and by the unbelieving Gentiles, as is described in part in the Acts of the Apostles and is set out more fully in the chronicles, histories and legends of the Saints. The Jews assailed her both by citing the Scriptures of the Old Testament and by actual persecution. So too the Gentile philosophers fought against the Church in various ways by natural reason; while kings and tyrants did so with the material sword. And as the Bridegroom foretold, those who believed in him were betrayed by parents, brethren, kinsmen and friends, and were put to death by them [see Luke 21:16]. Moreover, the universal Church in the person of the particular Churches, that is, any particular Church, can say: [[1:5|the sons of my mother|Filii matris meæ]], that is, the heretics who for a time were sons of the universal Church (of whom the apostle John says in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us|Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis]]), [[1:5|have fought against me|pugnaverunt contra me]], because they were very hostile to Catholics, above all the Arians, who also for many years persecuted and slaughtered the faithful in body. So too wicked Christians, schismatics, unjust princes and vicious prelates fight against the Church, by harassing the just, by scandalizing the little ones and their subjects, by stirring up unjust wars, or by not obeying the commands of the Church. And truly our loving mother the Church, who is ceaselessly and most grievously assailed by evil spirits and by unbelieving peoples, is not a little saddened when she sees her sons, who ought to help one another against those fiercest enemies just named, fighting against their own mother and against one another.

paras.t: Posuerunt me custodem in vineis : id est, infideles Judæi me in terra sua persequendo, atque ex ea me repellendo, fuerunt occasio, quod cœpi per totam gentilitatem dispergi, atque gentilibus toto orbe terrarum evangelizare: in quibus innumerabilia millia paganorum converti, et multas fundavi particulares Ecclesias, tanquam vineas Dei, quas pastorali sollicitudine custodivi, excolui, fecundavi. Hinc in apostolicis Actis Paulus et Barnabas obduratis loquuntur Judæis: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes: sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus, Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ. Vineam meam non custodivi : id est, Synagogam mihi commissam juste reliqui : et hoc, propter obstinationem, rebellionem, et incorrigibilitatem ipsius. Primitivæ namque Ecclesiæ, id est Apostolis et eorum adjutoribus, jussit Christus primo prædicare Judæis. Nam ante passionem suam præcepit : In viam gentium ne abieritis; sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel. Post resurrectionem vero præcepit eisdem Apostolis : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Nihilo minus intentio Christi fuit, ut adhuc primo ad tempus prædicarent Judæis : quod et pene per tredecim annos fecerunt pro majori parte ipsi gloriosi Apostoli, quousque divisi sunt. Interim tamen a tempore persecutionis factæ sub Stephano, sub qua (præter Apostolos) omnes discipuli fuerunt dispersi, coeperunt per totam Galilæam atque Samariam prædicare, sicut et Paulus ac Barnabas alibi : attamen Judæis dumtaxat, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum manifeste habetur. Tandem Judæis undique obduratis, ad gentilium conversionem profecti sunt.
paras.en: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews, by persecuting me in their land and driving me out of it, were the occasion of my beginning to be scattered through the whole Gentile world and to preach the Gospel to the Gentiles throughout the world; among whom I converted countless thousands of pagans and founded many particular Churches, as vineyards of God, which I kept, tilled and made fruitful with pastoral care. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles Paul and Barnabas say to the hardened Jews: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes]]: [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus]], [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ]] [the margin gives both Acts 13:46–47 and Is. xlix, 6, which the Apostles are quoting; Denis's "my salvation" follows Isaias]. [[1:5|my vineyard I have not kept|Vineam meam non custodivi]]: that is, I justly left the Synagogue entrusted to me, and this because of its obstinacy, rebellion and incorrigibility. For Christ commanded the early Church, that is, the Apostles and their helpers, to preach first to the Jews. For before his passion he commanded: [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]]; [[Matt 10:6|But go ye rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel|sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel]]. But after the resurrection he commanded the same Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. Nevertheless it was Christ's intention that they should still preach first to the Jews for a time; and this the glorious Apostles themselves did for the most part for nearly thirteen years, until they were separated. In the meantime, however, from the time of the persecution raised under Stephen, in which all the disciples except the Apostles were scattered[[Acts 8:1||]], they began to preach through all Galilee and Samaria, as did Paul and Barnabas elsewhere, yet to the Jews only, as is plainly found in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 13:46||]]. At last, when the Jews were hardened everywhere, they set out to convert the Gentiles.

paras.t: Insuper Ecclesia ex persona carnalium ac negligentium prælatorum dicere potest : Posuerunt me custodem in vineis: id est, Christus et ejus Apostoli præceperunt mihi, cum omni diligentia præsidere ac providere particularibus Ecclesiis Dei. Sic namque princeps Apostolorum hortatur : Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei. Et Paulus : Qui præest, in sollicitudine, supple, præsit. Vineam meam, id est vineas mihi commissas, non custodivi : per singulare intelligendo plurale, ut moris est in Scripturis.
paras.en: Moreover, the Church can say in the person of carnal and negligent prelates: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, Christ and his Apostles commanded me to preside over and provide for the particular Churches of God with all diligence. For so the prince of the Apostles exhorts: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei]]. And Paul: [[Rom 12:8|he that ruleth, with carefulness|Qui præest, in sollicitudine]], supply: let him rule. [[1:5|my vineyard|Vineam meam]], that is, the vineyards entrusted to me, [[1:5|I have not kept|non custodivi]]: understanding the plural by the singular, as is the custom in the Scriptures.

paras.t: Circa hæc ait Anselmus : Quemadmodum vineæ quatuor modis læduntur præcipue, sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ totidem adversa, maxime in suis membris teneris, solent nocere. Vineæ etenim obest asperum frigus, et urens ventus, spissaque grando, et nimia pluvia. Sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ in suis membris aliquando nocet frigus seu torpor exemplorum malorum: quoniam sicut frigus seu gelu stringit atque exterminat vineæ florem, sic malum exemplum aufert a tenero corde conceptæ devotionis amorem. Aliquando etiam ei obest ventus diabolicæ suggestionis, adurens renes mentis et corporis. Nocere etiam maxime solet grando pessimæ detractionis et dissensionis, quæ dissipat florem fraternæ dilectionis. Pluvia quoque pravæ doctrinæ, et prosperitatis assiduæ, solet plerumque statum mentis dissolvere, et ad amorem mundi reflectere. Sicut e contrario prodest vineæ suavis aura cum dulci rore, sic prodest Ecclesiæ pax cum salubri sermone. Præterea, sicut vinitores non custodiunt vineas, qui eas non putant, non considerant, non excolunt, nec fructum ex eis colligere conantur; ita prælati qui sibi commissis pravos mores, inordinata colloquia, opera illicita non præcidunt, nec qualiter subditi circa divinorum observantiam præceptorum se habeant, intuentur; nec corripiendo, corrigendo, exhortando, docendo, obsecrando, comminando, et orando pro eis, reformare eos conantur, neque exemplis neque verbis satagunt fructum virtutum et spiritualem assiduumque profectum ex ipsis producere, nequaquam ut tenentur vineas Dei commissas sibi custodiunt. Ideo sanguinem pereuntium Dominus requiret ab eis.
paras.en: On these words Anselm says: As vineyards are harmed chiefly in four ways, so the same number of adversities are wont to harm holy Church, above all in her tender members. For a vineyard is harmed by bitter cold, scorching wind, thick hail and too much rain. So holy Church is sometimes harmed in her members by the cold or numbness of bad examples: for as cold or frost nips and destroys the flower of the vine, so a bad example takes from a tender heart the love of the devotion it had conceived. Sometimes too she is harmed by the wind of the devil's suggestion, scorching the reins of mind and body. The hail of most wicked detraction and dissension is also wont to do the greatest harm, for it scatters the flower of brotherly love. The rain too of false doctrine and of constant prosperity often loosens the state of the mind and turns it back to the love of the world. As, on the contrary, a gentle breeze with sweet dew does good to the vineyard, so peace with wholesome preaching does good to the Church. Further, as vinedressers do not keep their vineyards who do not prune them, do not look to them, do not till them, and do not try to gather fruit from them; so prelates who do not cut away the evil manners, disorderly talk and unlawful works of those entrusted to them, nor look to how their subjects stand in keeping God's commandments, nor try to reform them by rebuking, correcting, exhorting, teaching, beseeching, threatening and praying for them, nor take pains by example or by word to bring forth from them the fruit of virtues and steady spiritual progress, by no means keep the vineyards of God entrusted to them as they are bound to. Therefore the Lord will require the blood of those who perish at their hands[[Ezech 33:6||]][[Ezech 33:8||]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam primitiva Ecclesia a Judæis dispersa, et per gentilitatem divisa, innumerabiles persecutiones sustinuit, sicut et Paulus in suis epistolis de se patefecit, recte subjungit Ecclesia : Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie : id est, tu, sponse cœlestis super omnia prædilecte, mihi dignanter ostende ubi tu gratiose commoreris, in quorum cordibus pabula internæ refectionis exhibeas, quos pastoraliter nutris. Indica etiam mihi ubi cubes, id est, stabiliter requiescas, quorum mentes tibi carissimas luce contemplationis perfundas : ita quod per contemplativæ exercitia vitæ, te intra se jugiter complectuntur, retinent, nec offendunt, ita ut illud Deuteronomii impleatur in eis : Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet.
paras.en: But since the early Church, scattered by the Jews and spread through the Gentile world, endured countless persecutions, as Paul too makes known of himself in his epistles[[2 Cor 11:23||]] [the margin gives II Cor. xi, 23–27], the Church rightly adds: [[1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]]: that is, thou, heavenly Bridegroom, beloved above all things, graciously show me where thou dost dwell in thy grace, in whose hearts thou dost set the food of inward refreshment, whom thou dost feed as a shepherd. [[1:6|Shew me|Indica mihi]] also [[1:6|where thou liest|ubi cubes]], that is, where thou dost steadfastly rest: whose minds, most dear to thee, thou dost flood with the light of contemplation, so that through the exercises of the contemplative life they hold thee constantly embraced within them, keep thee, and do not offend thee; so that that word of Deuteronomy is fulfilled in them: [[Deut 33:12|The best beloved of the Lord shall dwell confidently in him: as in a bride chamber shall he abide all the day long, and between his shoulders shall be rest|Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet]].

1.t: MULTIFARIE multisque modis Deus Pater, omnipotens, æternus, ab exordio mundi per verba et signa, per visiones, figuras, oracula, unigenitum suum Filium prædixit incarnandum, ac liberaturum genus humanum. Et hoc ipsum in lege naturæ ab Adam usque ad Moysen et legis scriptæ collationem, cognoverunt præcipui Patriarchæ et sancti viri, Adam, Seth, Enoch, Noe, Sem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, multique alii homines virtuosi, ex revelatione divina aut patrum suorum narratione : qui omnes Salvatoris adventum et Christi incarnationem, apparitionem, redemptionemque mundi ardentius optaverunt, quam æstimare valemus. Denique in monte Sinai revelata sunt desuper Moysi mysteria Christi, et qualiter de Christo facta fuit promissio illa, In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes, non solum Abrahæ, sed etiam Isaac et Jacob, prout in Genesi Moyses ipse descripsit. Postea vero sub lege per David, Salomonem, Isaiam, aliosque Prophetas prænuntiata et descripta sunt mysteria Salvatoris multo diffusius, quam sub lege naturæ : ita quod Judæi sub lege Moysis communiter crediderunt explicite, Salvatorem generis humani venturum in mundum. Quod totum constat ex eo, quod Christus in Evangelio suis ait discipulis : Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis. Dico enim vobis, quod multi reges et Prophetæ et justi voluerunt videre quæ vos videtis, et non viderunt, et audire quæ auditis, et non audierunt.
1.en: [[Heb 1:1|At sundry times and in divers manners|MULTIFARIE multisque modis]] God the Father, almighty and eternal, from the beginning of the world foretold, by words and signs, by visions, figures and oracles, that His only-begotten Son would become incarnate and would set mankind free. And this very thing was known under the law of nature, from Adam until Moses and the giving of the written law, to the chief Patriarchs and holy men, Adam, Seth, Enoch, Noe, Sem, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and many other virtuous men, by divine revelation or by what their fathers told them: and all of them longed for the coming of the Saviour, and for the incarnation of Christ, His appearing and the redemption of the world, more ardently than we are able to reckon. Then on Mount Sinai the mysteries of Christ were revealed from on high to Moses, and how that promise, [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations|In semine tuo]] [[Gen 22:18|be blessed|benedicentur omnes gentes]][[Gen 26:4||]][[Gen 28:14||]], was made concerning Christ, not to Abraham only but also to Isaac and Jacob, as Moses himself described in Genesis. Afterwards, under the law, the mysteries of the Saviour were foretold and described far more fully through David, Solomon, Isaias and the other Prophets than under the law of nature: so that the Jews under the law of Moses commonly believed explicitly that the Saviour of mankind would come into the world. All of which is plain from this, that Christ says to His disciples in the Gospel: [[Luke 10:23|Blessed are the eyes that see the things which you see|Beati oculi qui vident quæ vos videtis]]. [[Luke 10:24|For I say to you that many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see and have not seen them; and to hear the things that you hear and have not heard them|Dico enim vobis, quod multi reges et Prophetæ et justi voluerunt videre quæ vos videtis, et non viderunt, et audire quæ auditis, et non audierunt]] [Denis reads "many kings and prophets and just men"].

1.t: Itaque in persona universorum illorum fidelium, qui sub lege naturæ legeque scripta fuerunt, et Christi adventum ardentissime cupierunt, nunc dicitur : Osculetur me osculo oris sui : id est, Salvator mundi, Filius Dei, mihi tam diu totiesque promissus, per incarnationis mysterium personaliter veniat, naturam meam in unitate personæ assumat, se ipsum mihi facie ad faciem repræsentet, ore ad os mihi loquatur, inter homines conversetur : sicque in medio terræ meam operetur salutem. Denique, quam æstuanter Sancti antiqui istud desideraverunt, perpendere possumus : Primo ex dignitate et excellentia sponsi istius, cujus nobilitas est immensa, speciositas infinita, sapientia prorsus interminabilis, opulentia illimitabilis, incircumscripta suavitas, supercopiosissima pietas, et beatitudo sine termino et mensura. Non itaque mirum, si tali ac tanto tam infinitæ excellentiæ atque dulcedinis sponso, optavit uniri et desponsari hæc sponsa. Secundo id ipsum perpendere possumus ex magnitudine indigentiæ sponsæ istius. Erat namque damnata exsilio, ejecta de paradiso, jugo peccati gravata, servituti ac potestati diaboli aliquo modo subjecta, atque æternæ beatitudinis jucunditatibus destituta ; in lacum miseriæ lutumque fœcis erat projecta, nec erat qui manum porrigeret adjutricem, per subventionem completam et redemptionem finalem. Tertio idem pensare valemus ex miro, copioso et saluberrimo fructu, qui provenit Ecclesiæ ex prætacto osculo sponsi istius : quia per ipsum a cunctis malis præinductis est liberata, ad sanctam libertatem reducta, amica, sponsa, filia, hæres, consors sui Creatoris effecta, charismatibus gratiarum mirifice decorata. Per ipsum facta est gens sancta, populus acquisitionis, genus electum, regale sacerdotium, præ cunctis nationibus gloriosa.
1.en: And so, in the person of all those faithful who lived under the law of nature and under the written law, and who most ardently longed for the coming of Christ, it is now said: [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]]: that is, may the Saviour of the world, the Son of God, so long and so often promised to me, come in person through the mystery of the incarnation; may He take up my nature into the unity of His person, show Himself to me face to face, speak to me mouth to mouth, and dwell among men: and so work my salvation in the midst of the earth[[Ps 73:12||]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxiii, 12; the words are from Ps 73:12, "he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth"]. Now how burningly the holy men of old desired this, we can weigh: First, from the dignity and excellence of this Bridegroom, whose nobility is immeasurable, His beauty infinite, His wisdom altogether without bound, His riches without limit, His sweetness uncircumscribed, His goodness superabundant, and His beatitude without end or measure. It is no wonder, then, if this bride longed to be united and espoused to such and so great a Bridegroom, of so infinite an excellence and sweetness. Secondly, we can weigh the same from the greatness of this bride's need. For she was condemned to exile, cast out of paradise, weighed down by the yoke of sin, in some manner subject to the servitude and power of the devil, and stripped of the delights of eternal beatitude; she had been thrown into [[Ps 39:3|the pit of misery and the mire of dregs|lacum miseriæ lutumque fœcis]], and there was none to stretch out a helping hand by a full relief and a final redemption. Thirdly, we can consider the same from the wonderful, abundant and most wholesome fruit that came to the Church from the aforesaid kiss of this Bridegroom: for by it she was set free from all the evils brought upon her before, led back to holy liberty, made the friend, the bride, the daughter, the heir and the partner of her Creator, and wonderfully adorned with the gifts of graces. By it she was made [[1 Pet 2:9|a holy nation, a purchased people|gens sancta, populus acquisitionis]], [[1 Pet 2:9|a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood|genus electum, regale sacerdotium]], glorious above all nations.

1.t: Præterea, sicut in sponso isto, Domino Jesu Christo, est duplex natura, divina videlicet et humana, ita et duplex os, puta divinum et increatum, humanumque et creatum. Os Christi divinum et increatum, est intellectus seu sapientia ejus æterna, per quam loquitur omni menti bene dispositæ, juxta illud Psalmistæ : Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus. In Job quoque legitur : Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit. Unde quibusdam improperat per Prophetam, dicentem : Væ, filii desertores, ut faceretis consilium, et non ex me, et os meum non interrogastis. Amplius, hoc increato ore suo loquitur Unigenitus Dei universis Beatis in patria immediate ea, quæ ad essentiale præmium pertinent eorumdem. Nempe hæc locutio non est nisi manifestatio qua eis ostendit clare se ipsum, seu divinam essentiam, ad intuendum ac perfruendum. Estque locutio ista toti supergloriosissimæ Trinitati communis, quemadmodum et idem numero intellectus est in tribus adorandis superdignissimisque Personis. Actiones etenim Dei ad extra, communes sunt summæ et individuæ Trinitati. De effectibus autem suis loquitur Verbum æternum quædam immediate superioribus angelicis mentibus, per quas et inferiores angelicas illuminat mentes de talibus; et per sanctos angelos loquitur inde hominibus : prout in libris de Angelica et Ecclesiastica hierarchiis docet Dionysius Magnus.
1.en: Moreover, as in this Bridegroom, the Lord Jesus Christ, there is a twofold nature, namely divine and human, so there is also a twofold mouth, divine and uncreated, and human and created. The divine and uncreated mouth of Christ is His eternal understanding or wisdom, by which He speaks to every well-disposed mind, according to that word of the Psalmist: [[Ps 84:9|I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me|Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus]]. In Job too we read: [[Job 33:14|God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time|Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo id ipsum non repetit]]. Hence He reproaches certain men through the Prophet, who says: [[Is 30:1|Woe to you, apostate children|Væ, filii desertores]], [[Is 30:1|that you would take counsel, and not of me|ut faceretis consilium, et non ex me]], and [[Is 30:2|have not asked at my mouth|os meum non interrogastis]]. Further, with this uncreated mouth of His the Only-begotten of God speaks immediately to all the Blessed in the fatherland the things that belong to their essential reward [that is, the vision of God itself, as distinct from the accidental joys added to it]. For this speaking is nothing other than the manifestation by which He shows Himself, that is, the divine essence, clearly to them, to behold and to enjoy. And this speaking is common to the whole most supremely glorious Trinity, just as the understanding is one and the same in number in the three adorable and most supremely worthy Persons. For the works of God outside Himself are common to the supreme and undivided Trinity. But concerning His effects the eternal Word speaks certain things immediately to the higher angelic minds, through which He also enlightens the lower angelic minds about such things; and through the holy angels He then speaks to men: as Dionysius the Great teaches in the books On the Angelic and the Ecclesiastical Hierarchies.

1.t: Itaque, dum Verbum æternum, Unigenitus Dei, sibi ipsi conjunxit naturam humanam hypostatica unione, assumendo eam ad suum esse personale æternum et increatum, tunc immediate tetigit, circumplexus et osculatus est eam, et per eam osculatus est omnes nos. Propter quod ad Hebræos scribit Apostolus : Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit. Deinde visus in terris, et cum hominibus conversatus, osculatus est nos, per se ipsum alloquendo, instruendo, consolando fideles, eosque Deo Patri reconciliando. Denique discipulos suos ad se redeuntes consuevit in osculo sancto etiam corporali recipere. Unde per Zachariam prophetam prædixit: Gaude et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui; et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa. Hinc etiam in alio Propheta fuit prædictum: Qui fecit stellas, hic est Deus noster; hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ, et dedit illam Jacob puero suo, et Israel dilecto suo. Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est.
1.en: And so, when the eternal Word, the Only-begotten of God, joined human nature to Himself by the hypostatic union [that is, the union of the two natures in the one Person of the Word], taking it up into His own eternal and uncreated personal being, He then touched it immediately, embraced it and kissed it, and through it He kissed all of us. For this reason the Apostle writes to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:16|nowhere doth he take hold of the angels: but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold|Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit]]. Then, seen upon earth and conversing with men[[Bar 3:38||]], He kissed us, by speaking to the faithful Himself, instructing and consoling them, and reconciling them to God the Father. And He was accustomed to receive His disciples, when they came back to Him, with a holy kiss, even a bodily one. Hence He foretold through the prophet Zacharias: [[Zach 2:10|Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion: for behold I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee|Gaude et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui]] [Denis reads Gaude, "rejoice", for "sing praise"]; [[Zach 2:11|And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day|et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa]]. Hence it was also foretold in another Prophet: He that made the stars[[Bar 3:35||]], [[Bar 3:36|This is our God|hic est Deus noster]]; [[Bar 3:37|He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it to Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved|hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ, et dedit illam Jacob puero suo, et Israel dilecto suo]]. [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]

1.t: Quæri etiam potest, qualiter Ecclesia humilis, ausa fuit tantæ majestatis sponsi osculum flagitare, cui exercitus cœli cum tremore adsistit, quem Cherubim Seraphimque adorant; de quo in Job legitur: Magnus fortitudine, et judicio, et justitia; et enarrari non potest: ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui videntur sibi esse sapientes. Ad quod breviter respondendum, quod duo specialiter incitaverunt Ecclesiam ad postulandum nuptiale hoc osculum. Primum, quoniam ipse benignissimus sponsus tam gratiose eam prævenit, suam incarnationem et adventum ei prænuntiando ac promittendo: et ex hoc ipsa concepit fiduciam id petendi. Secundum fuit ardentissima caritas Ecclesiæ ad hunc sponsum. Caritas autem, separationis impatiens est, unionisque avida, et frequenter prædominando rationem transcendit; et ingerit se dilecto, quem quanto æstuantius amat, tanto propinquius, imo et intimius appetit ei uniri: ac grandem parit fiduciam, respicitque dilectum potius ut dilectum, quam ut dominum aut majorem. Potest addi et tertium, videlicet magnitudo necessitatis, quæ lege non stringitur. Indiguit enim vehementissime salvatore, nec salvari potuit nisi per istiusmodi sponsum.
1.en: It may also be asked how the lowly Church dared to beg for the kiss of a Bridegroom of such majesty, before whom the host of heaven stands with trembling, whom the Cherubim and Seraphim adore; of whom we read in Job: [[Job 37:23|great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable|Magnus fortitudine, et judicio, et justitia; et enarrari non potest]]: [[Job 37:24|Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him|ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui videntur sibi esse sapientes]]. To this the short answer is that two things in particular moved the Church to ask for this nuptial kiss. The first, that this most kind Bridegroom Himself so graciously went before her, foretelling and promising her His incarnation and coming: and from this she conceived the confidence to ask for it. The second was the Church's most ardent charity towards this Bridegroom. Now charity cannot bear separation and is eager for union, and often, prevailing, it goes beyond reason; and it presses itself upon the beloved, and the more burningly it loves him, the more closely, nay the more intimately, it longs to be united to him: and it begets great confidence, and looks upon the beloved rather as beloved than as lord or superior. A third may be added, namely the greatness of her need, which is bound by no law. For she needed a saviour most urgently, and could not be saved except through such a Bridegroom.

1.t: Consequenter sponsa hæc, universalis Ecclesia, causam aperit suæ petitionis, et a tertia persona convertitur ad secundam, et eum jam alloquitur quasi præsentem, dicendo: quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino: de quo, tanquam de absente, præmisit, Osculetur me osculo oris sui. Quæ enim suspiriose cupit cœlestis sponsi præsentiam, eo ipso quo sic ad ipsum afficitur, aliqualem ejus præsentiam mox meretur: siquidem prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate. Noverat quoque hæc sponsa sponsum suum, nec loco, nec tempore circumscribi, sed esse ubique præsentem.
1.en: Next this bride, the universal Church, discloses the reason for her petition, and turns from the third person to the second, and now addresses Him as though present, saying: [[1:1|for thy breasts are better than wine|quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino]]: Him of whom, as of one absent, she had said before, [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]]. For she who longs with sighs for the presence of the heavenly Bridegroom, by the very fact that she is so moved towards Him, soon merits some presence of His: since [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him: to all that call upon him in truth|prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate]]. This bride knew, too, that her Bridegroom is not circumscribed by place or by time, but is present everywhere.

1.t: Ideo ut præsentem confidenter alloquitur: et quæ quasi orando dixit ad Patrem sponsi sui æternum, Osculetur me osculo oris sui, o Pater æterne, Unigenitus tuus; mox sponsi amore plus quam ante succensa, non quivit diutius ab ejus alloquio abstinere. Nempe qui ardentissime amat, sui sermonis variat modum ac ordinem, secundum diversum sui amoris impulsum ac tactum et flammam. Ideo super Cantica asserit Alexander: Modum sui sermonis non continet amor, directo tenore non graditur.
1.en: Therefore she addresses Him confidently as present: and she who, as though in prayer, had said to the eternal Father of her Bridegroom, [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]], that is, O eternal Father, let Thy Only-begotten do so, soon, kindled with love of the Bridegroom more than before, could no longer keep from speaking to Him. For one who loves most ardently varies the manner and order of his speech according to the varying impulse, touch and flame of his love. Hence Alexander says on the Canticles: Love does not keep to one manner of speech; it does not walk on a straight course.

1.t: Itaque ait: Meliora sunt ubera tua vino. Per ubera sponsi, secundum Origenem, intelliguntur arcana cordis seu pectoris Christi, hoc est thesauri sapientiæ et scientiæ in ipso absconditi, quibus alit suorum corda fidelium. Possunt quoque per duo ubera sponsi, intelligi duo caritatis præcepta; item vetus Testamentum spiritualiter intellectum, ac novum; et rursus præcepta Salvatoris, et evangelica ejus consilia; similiter misericordia ejus et veritas; itemque gratia præveniens, et subsequens. Hæc ubera meliora sunt vino, id est doctrina legis ac Prophetarum, et rigore contento in lege, litteralique sensu ipsius, atque cærimonialibus ac judicialibus legis præceptis. Magna equidem est eminentia evangelicæ legis, quæ est lex caritatis, et gratiam continens ac conferens, et opere exhibens quod prædicebatur ac promittebatur in lege atque Prophetis, super ipsam legem, quæ fuit lex timoris, nec gratiam continebat, ac nihil ad perfectum adduxit. Ideo in Evangelio Joannis scribitur: Lex per Moysen data est; gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est. Propter quod tempus evangelicæ legis, tempus gratiæ nuncupatur.
1.en: And so she says: [[1:1|thy breasts are better than wine|Meliora sunt ubera tua vino]]. By the Bridegroom's breasts, according to Origen, are understood the secrets of the heart or breast of Christ, that is, the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden in Him, with which He feeds the hearts of His faithful. By the two breasts of the Bridegroom may also be understood the two precepts of charity; likewise the Old Testament spiritually understood, and the New; and again the precepts of the Saviour and His evangelical counsels; similarly His mercy and truth; and likewise prevenient and subsequent grace [that is, the grace that goes before the will and moves it, and the grace that accompanies and follows its consent]. These [[1:1|breasts are better than wine|ubera meliora sunt vino]], that is, than the teaching of the law and the Prophets, than the rigour contained in the law and its literal sense, and than the ceremonial and judicial precepts of the law. Great indeed is the pre-eminence of the law of the Gospel, which is the law of charity, containing and conferring grace, and showing in deed what was foretold and promised in the law and the Prophets, over the law itself, which was the law of fear, did not contain grace, and [[Heb 7:19|brought nothing to perfection|nihil ad perfectum adduxit]]. Therefore it is written in the Gospel of John: [[John 1:17|the law was given by Moses: grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Lex per Moysen data est; gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est]]. For this reason the time of the law of the Gospel is called the time of grace.

1.t: Fragrantia unguentis optimis, id est pretiosissimis charismatibus gratiæ ac virtutum, ac sacro septenario Spiritus Sancti : quibus Christus secundum naturam assumptam fuit excellentissime inunctus, repletus et fragrans, sicut per Isaiam testatur : Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me. Cui cantamus in Psalmo : Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ præ participibus tuis. De quo in Actibus Apostolorum sacratissimus princeps Apostolorum fatetur : Unxit eum Deus Spiritu Sancto et virtute. Insuper ubera Christi, id est documenta, præcepta, et evangelica ejus consilia, fragrant optimis unguentis, id est ecclesiasticis sacramentis : quæ sunt medicinalia vasa gratiarum cœlestium contentiva, quibus præceptorum violationes curantur, et quorum auxilio ipsa præcepta atque consilia prompto animo adimplentur : quæ optima unguenta ex fonte pectoris sponsi fluxerunt, imo et ex ejus latere in cruce perforato emanasse dicuntur.
1.en: [[1:2|Smelling sweet of the best ointments|Fragrantia unguentis optimis]], that is, of the most precious gifts of grace and of the virtues, and of the sacred sevenfold gift of the Holy Ghost: with which Christ, according to the nature He assumed, was most excellently anointed, filled and fragrant, as He testifies through Isaias: [[Is 61:1|The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me|Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me]] [Denis omits "the Lord" before "hath anointed"]. To whom we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:8|God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows|Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ præ participibus tuis]]. Of whom the most holy prince of the Apostles declares in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 10:38|God anointed him with the Holy Ghost and with power|Unxit eum Deus Spiritu Sancto et virtute]]. Moreover, the breasts of Christ, that is, His teachings, precepts and evangelical counsels, smell sweet of the best ointments, that is, of the sacraments of the Church: which are healing vessels containing heavenly graces, by which violations of the precepts are cured, and by whose help the precepts and counsels themselves are fulfilled with a ready mind: and these best ointments flowed from the fountain of the Bridegroom's breast, nay, they are said to have streamed from His side pierced on the cross.

1.t: Circa hunc locum scribit quidam specialiter super illud, Quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino : In Hebræo habetur, Quia meliores sunt amores tui. Nomen enim Hebraicum hic positum, est æquivocum ad amores et ad ubera. Hebræi sequuntur unam significationem, translatio nostra aliam. Sed in hoc Hebræi videntur melius dicere, quia secundum proprietatem Hebraici sermonis, sponsa hic alloquitur sponsum. In commendatione autem sponsi, non videtur convenienter mentio fieri de uberibus. Est igitur sensus secundum Hebræos, quod amores sponsi sunt sapidiores menti devotæ, quam quodcumque sapidum corporale gustui corporali. — Circa hæc reor dicendum, quia si nomen illud Hebraicum est ad utrumque istud æquivocum, non potius habetur in Hebræo, Amores, quam, Ubera. Insuper videtur dicendum, quod Hieronymus aptius transtulit Ubera, ad insinuandum quod spiritualis sit intellectus, non sensus carnalis. Spiritualia etenim ubera, magis conveniunt sponso quam sponsæ, imo et uberibus sui alitur sponsi : et istud Cassiodorus tangit. Amplius Occam allegat Augustinum dicentem, quod viris proprie conveniunt mamillæ, feminis mammæ, pecoribus ubera : imo ubera pro mamillis et mammis accipi solent : sicque asserit Hugo, quod ubera data sunt viris in corporis ornamentum, non ad necessitatem. Ergo et ubera proprie competunt sponso : et certe sponsa in sponso libenter commemorat quod ipsa in se ipsa esse cognoscit, quatenus ex amborum similitudine, amor validius accendatur.
1.en: On this place someone writes, specially on the words [[1:1|for thy breasts are better than wine|Quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino]]: In the Hebrew it reads, For thy loves are better. For the Hebrew word set here is ambiguous between "loves" and "breasts" [the Hebrew dodim, "loves", and dadim, "breasts", are written with the same letters]. The Hebrews follow one meaning, our translation the other. But in this the Hebrews seem to say it better, since according to the idiom of the Hebrew tongue the bride is here addressing the Bridegroom, and in praising a bridegroom it does not seem fitting to mention breasts. So the sense according to the Hebrews is that the Bridegroom's loves are more savoury to the devout mind than anything savoury in the body is to the bodily taste. On this I think it must be said that, if that Hebrew word is ambiguous between the two, the Hebrew no more reads "loves" than "breasts". Further it seems right to say that Jerome more fittingly translated "breasts", to suggest that the understanding is spiritual, not a carnal sense. For spiritual breasts belong to the Bridegroom more than to the bride, nay she herself is fed at the breasts of her Bridegroom: and Cassiodorus touches on this. Moreover Occam cites Augustine as saying that mamillæ properly belong to men, mammæ to women, and ubera to cattle [three Latin words for breasts or teats, which English cannot tell apart]: yet ubera are commonly taken for both mamillæ and mammæ: and so Hugh says that breasts were given to men as an ornament of the body, not for need. Therefore breasts too properly befit the Bridegroom: and surely the bride gladly recalls in the Bridegroom what she knows to be in herself, so that from the likeness of the two, love may be kindled the more strongly.

1.t: Denique adhuc sponsi laudibus immoratur, et cur ejus osculum cupiat reserans, protestatur : Oleum effusum nomen tuum : id est, non solum tu ipse, o sponse, instar olei fusi, suavis et splendidus es; sed et nomen tuum, quodcumque sit illud, dulciter resonat in auribus meis, et ex sola nuncupatione tua dulcescit anima mea, reficitur, exhilaratur, clarescit. Insuper nomen tuum, id est fama excellentiæ tuæ toto orbe terrarum diffusa, fulget ac redolet, estque bonus odor Dei Patris, imo totius superpræstantissimæ Trinitatis in omni loco : sed et prædicatio majestatis tuæ coruscat, suaviterque odorat ut oleum vase fusum; et sicut oleum ceteris humoribus supernatat, sic nomen tuum præeminet universis. Quemadmodum etiam oleum ceteris cibis fert condimentum, influitque saporem, sic nomen tuum condimentum est Scripturarum, et spiritualibus eduliis animarum confert suavitatem. Rursus, sicut oleum lenit dolores ac vulnera sanat, sic nomen tuum, o sponse cœlestis, fugat a corde mœrorem, et vitiorum læsioni medetur.
1.en: Then she lingers still on the praises of the Bridegroom, and, disclosing why she desires His kiss, declares: [[1:2|Thy name is as oil poured out|Oleum effusum nomen tuum]]: that is, not only art Thou Thyself, O Bridegroom, sweet and shining like oil poured out; but Thy name too, whatever it be, sounds sweetly in my ears, and at the mere naming of Thee my soul grows sweet, is refreshed, gladdened and brightened. Moreover Thy name, that is, the fame of Thy excellence spread through the whole world, shines and gives forth its fragrance, and is the good odour of God the Father, nay of the whole most supremely excellent Trinity, in every place[[2 Cor 2:15||]] ["in every place" is from the verse before, 2 Cor 2:14]: and the preaching of Thy majesty glitters, and smells sweet like oil poured from a vessel; and as oil floats above all other liquids, so Thy name stands above all things. And as oil gives seasoning to other foods and imparts flavour, so Thy name is the seasoning of the Scriptures, and lends sweetness to the spiritual food of souls. Again, as oil soothes pains and heals wounds, so Thy name, O heavenly Bridegroom, drives grief from the heart and heals the hurt of vices.

1.t: De salubritate nominis hujus, angelus sanctus dixit ad Joseph : Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. Siquidem Jesus interpretatur salvator : qui in Isaia sic effatur : Deus justus et salvans non est præter me. Atque in alio Propheta : Ego Dominus Deus tuus; et salvator non est præter me. Etenim Domino Jesu Christo secundum suam deitatem convenit salvare, propria et increata auctoritate et potestate : cui ex divina natura convenit peccata dimittere, dona gratiarum per creationem infundere, beatitudinemque æternam largiri. Porro secundum assumptam humanitatem, convenit ei salvare, ut causæ instrumentali, meritoriæ, eminenti, et tanquam mediatori ac satisfactori. Nam sicut corpus nostrum comparatur ad animam nostram, ut animæ instrumentum conjunctum, animatum, et proprium : sic humanitas Christi comparatur ad ejus deitatem et ad Verbum æternum quod eam assumpsit, velut instrumentum ipsius deitatis ac Verbi immediatum, conjunctum, animatum, et proprium : ut asserit Damascenus. Insuper, quam singulare, salubre et efficax sit nomen sponsi istius, pandit princeps Apostolorum, sic dicens : Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri. De cujus nominis majestate Vas ait electionis : Dedit ei Deus Pater nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur cœlestium, terrestrium, et infernorum.
1.en: Of the saving power of this name the holy angel said to Joseph: [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus. For he shall save his people from their sins|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum; ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]. For Jesus means Saviour: who speaks thus in Isaias: [[Is 45:21|A just God and a saviour, there is none besides me|Deus justus et salvans non est præter me]]. And in another Prophet: [[Osee 13:4|I am the Lord thy God|Ego Dominus Deus tuus]]; [[Osee 13:4|and there is no saviour beside me|et salvator non est præter me]]. For to the Lord Jesus Christ according to His Godhead it belongs to save by His own uncreated authority and power: to whom, from the divine nature, it belongs to forgive sins, to pour in the gifts of graces by creation, and to bestow eternal beatitude. But according to the humanity He assumed, it belongs to Him to save as an instrumental, meritorious and pre-eminent cause, and as mediator and the one who makes satisfaction. For as our body is related to our soul as the soul's conjoined, living and proper instrument, so the humanity of Christ is related to His Godhead and to the eternal Word who assumed it, as the immediate, conjoined, living and proper instrument of that Godhead and Word: as Damascene says. Further, how singular, saving and effective the name of this Bridegroom is, the prince of the Apostles makes plain, saying: [[Acts 4:12|there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri]]. Of the majesty of this name the Vessel of election [that is, St Paul, so called in Acts 9:15] says: God the Father [[Phil 2:9|hath given him a name which is above all names|Dedit ei Deus Pater nomen, quod est super omne nomen]], [[Phil 2:10|That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth|ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur cœlestium, terrestrium, et infernorum]].

1.t: Præterea, Oleum effusum nomen tuum: id est, tu ipse, o illustrissime sponse, oleo compararis, et bonitas tua omni oleo exstat suavior, nobilitas tua omni oleo invenitur splendidior, unctio tua reficit mentes, pietas tua medetur animarum corporumque vulneribus, consolatio tua lenit pœnitentialem mærorem, et omnem inordinatam fugat tristitiam; ideo adolescentulæ dilexerunt te, id est particulares Ecclesiæ, et animæ spiritualiter renovatæ, atque incipientium mentes, et gentes olim paganæ, superbæ, carnales, inverecundæ, sed per gratiam tuam conversæ, et sobriæ, pudicæ, humilesque effectæ. Ad litteram quoque virgines sacræ, electæ puellæ, virtuosæ juvenculæ : quarum multæ pro tuo amore non solum totius mundi divitias, oblectamenta, honores, omnemque externum ornatum, vanitatem ac levitatem feminineam contempserunt; sed et crudelissima mortis genera virilissime pertulerunt, ac felicissime triumpharunt : quemadmodum sacratissima Catharina, præclarissima Ursula, et eis consimiles. Aliæ demum innumerabiles, in virginitate mentis ac corporis tibi constantissime servierunt ; et usque in præsens quasi innumeræ tales, in adolescentia sua relinquentes hoc sæculum nequam cum omni ejus fallacia, ingrediuntur cœnobia et reclusoria sancta, in quibus perpetuo clausæ manentes, tuis castissimis in spiritu vacant amplexibus.
1.en: Again, [[1:2|Thy name is as oil poured out|Oleum effusum nomen tuum]]: that is, Thou Thyself, O most illustrious Bridegroom, art likened to oil, and Thy goodness is sweeter than any oil, Thy nobility is found brighter than any oil, Thy anointing refreshes minds, Thy loving-kindness heals the wounds of souls and bodies, Thy consolation soothes the grief of penance and drives away all disordered sadness; [[1:2|therefore young maidens have loved thee|ideo adolescentulæ dilexerunt te]], that is, the particular Churches, and souls spiritually renewed, and the minds of beginners, and the nations once pagan, proud, carnal and shameless, but converted by Thy grace and made sober, chaste and humble. Literally also, sacred virgins, chosen maidens, virtuous young women: many of whom, for love of Thee, not only despised the riches, delights and honours of the whole world, and all outward adornment, and womanly vanity and lightness, but also bore the cruellest kinds of death most manfully, and triumphed most happily: like the most holy Catharine, the most illustrious Ursula, and others like them. Others again without number have served Thee most constantly in virginity of mind and body; and to this day such women, almost without number, leaving in their youth this wicked world with all its deceit, enter convents and holy anchorholds, in which, remaining enclosed for ever, they give themselves to Thy most chaste embraces in the spirit.

1.t: Trahe me post te. Istud in persona Ecclesiæ sub evangelica lege viventis, proprie sumitur : quæ sciens suum sponsum venisse, humanæ redemptionis mysteria complexisse, et ascendisse in cœlos, appetit sequi eum; sed recolens sponsum suum dixisse. Sine me nihil potestis facere, invocat gratiosum ejus auxilium, dicens : Trahe me post te, id est, excita et tolle meum torporem, accende in me tuæ caritatis ardorem, qui jugiter trahit sursum, quemadmodum ignis levatur in altum ; tuæ increatæ atque immensæ suavitatis sapore me affice, ut ad te solum pure jugiterque afficiar, tibi semper adhæream, ad te indesinenter adspirem : quatenus illam sancti tui Apostoli exhortationem adimpleam : Quæ sursum sunt quærite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei sedens; quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram. Scio enim te, Domine Jesu, dixisse : Si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum : et rursum. Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater, qui misit me, traxerit eum. Nec dubito quin Deus Pater tuus, et tu Unigenitus ejus, sitis unus tractor, sicut et unus creator. Rursus, novi vere ab Apostolo dictum : Non sumus sufficientes cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis: sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est.
1.en: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]]. This is properly taken in the person of the Church living under the law of the Gospel: knowing that her Bridegroom has come, has fulfilled the mysteries of man's redemption and has ascended into heaven, she longs to follow him; but remembering that her Bridegroom said, [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]], she calls on his gracious help, saying: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]]; that is, rouse and take away my sluggishness, kindle in me the ardour of thy charity, which ever draws upward, as fire rises on high; touch me with the savour of thy uncreated and boundless sweetness, so that I may be drawn purely and constantly to thee alone, cleave to thee always, and aspire to thee without ceasing; and so fulfil that exhortation of thy holy Apostle: [[Col 3:1|seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God|Quæ sursum sunt quærite, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei sedens]]; [[Col 3:2|Mind the things that are above, not the things that are upon the earth|quæ sursum sunt sapite, non quæ super terram]]. For I know, Lord Jesus, that thou hast said: [[John 12:32|if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]; and again: [[John 6:44|No man can come to me, except the Father, who hath sent me, draw him|Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater, qui misit me, traxerit eum]]. Nor do I doubt that God thy Father and thou his Only-begotten are one drawer, as you are also one Creator. Again, I know that the Apostle truly said: We are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|sufficientes cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis: sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]].

1.t: Ecce, o sponse cœlestis, dulcissime Jesu, conatur spiritus meus tibi fideliter adhærere, in te conquiescere, tibi per contemplationem amorosam et contemplativum amorem sincere vacare; sed retrahunt, retardant, impediunt mille impedimenta. Intellectus enim instabilis est, ratio debilis, voluntas ad vana ac mala proclivis, sensualitas trahit deorsum, quotidianæ necessitates in terrenis me occupant sensibilibusque involvunt, exteriorum sensuum objecta alliciunt, acies vitiorum, mundus, et dæmonum turbæ, undique nos impugnant : et certe ambulo in medio laqueorum, in agmine gravissimorum periculorum, sed et moles miseræ carnis me deprimit. Quid igitur mihi incumbit? nisi ad tuam confugere gratiosissimam opem, et ex intimo cordis affectu orare : Trahe me post te, incessabiliter tange, perfunde, illustra, adjuva et conforta cor meum. Tu enim per Osee prophetam dixisti : In funiculis Adam traham eos, in vinculis caritatis ; item per Jeremiam : In caritate perpetua dilexi te ; ideo attraxi te miserans. Prævaleat in me, Domine, tractus iste; absit semper longe a me omnis tractus adulterium affectionis, et omnis irrationabilium passionum, suspicionum ac vitiorum impulsus.
1.en: Behold, O heavenly Bridegroom, sweetest Jesus, my spirit strives to cleave faithfully to thee, to rest in thee, to give itself sincerely to thee through loving contemplation and contemplative love; but a thousand hindrances draw it back, slow it, and hinder it. For the understanding is unsteady, the reason weak, the will prone to vain and evil things; sensuality drags downward; daily needs busy me with earthly things and entangle me in things of sense; the objects of the outward senses allure; the battle line of the vices, the world and the hosts of demons assail us on every side. And truly I walk in the midst of snares, in a throng of the gravest dangers, and the weight of this wretched flesh too bears me down. What then is left to me, but to flee to thy most gracious help, and to pray from the inmost affection of the heart: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]]; touch, steep, enlighten, help and strengthen my heart without ceasing. For thou hast said by the prophet Osee: [[Osee 11:4|I will draw them with the cords of Adam, with the bands of love|In funiculis Adam traham eos, in vinculis caritatis]]; and likewise by Jeremias: [[Jer 31:3|I have loved thee with an everlasting love, therefore have I drawn thee, taking pity on thee|In caritate perpetua dilexi te ; ideo attraxi te miserans]]. Let this drawing prevail in me, O Lord; and far from me be always every drawing of adulterous affection, and every impulse of irrational passions, suspicions and vices.

1.t: Curremus in odore unguentorum tuorum : id est, si ita attraxeris me, ego et filiæ meæ ac animæ recenter conversæ, quibus gratiam mihi communicatam impertiri studebo, celeriter appropinquabimus tibi, et viam mandatorum tuorum curremus, igne amoris succensæ. Æstuanter quippe amanti nihil difficile, et ei qui gustavit quam multa sit abundantia dulcedinis tuæ, nihil molestius quam retardari a te, et a caritatis cursibus impediri. Curremus (inquam) in odore unguentorum tuorum, id est, affecti gustu interno supernorum charismatum, gratia et effectibus ecclesiasticorum sacramentorum, prægustatione cœlestium gaudiorum, affluentiaque donorum Spiritus Sancti. Hæc sunt unguenta valde suavia et præclara : ad quæ ut pertingere valeamus, oportet nos sequi vestigia in primis sanctæ humilitatis, patientiæ, mansuetudinis, passionisque Christi; et per veram contritionem cum beatissima Magdalene prosterni ad pedes sponsi cœlestis, eosque pœnitentiæ lacrimis ubertim lavare ac osculari; et inde per satisfactionem condignam, per spiritualem profectum, et jugem cordis custodiam, ad oscula manuum ejus consurgere : sicque ordinate per puræ ac fervidæ caritatis affectiones flammigeras, per incommutabilis Veritatis contemplationes sinceras, ad osculum oris ejus mundissimi cum summa veneratione accedere ; nec cum impiissimo traditore, polluta mente ad summæ Sanctitatis os deosculandum nos ipsos ingerere.
1.en: [[1:3|We will run|Curremus]] [[1:3|to the odour of thy ointments|in odore unguentorum tuorum]]: that is, if thou draw me so, I and my daughters, the newly converted souls to whom I shall strive to impart the grace given to me, will swiftly draw near to thee, and, set on fire with love, we shall run [[Ps 118:32|the way of thy commandments|viam mandatorum tuorum]]. For to one who loves ardently nothing is hard; and to one who has tasted how great is the abundance of thy sweetness[[Ps 30:20||]], nothing is more grievous than to be held back from thee and hindered in the courses of charity. [[1:3|We will run|Curremus]] (I say) [[1:3|to the odour of thy ointments|in odore unguentorum tuorum]]: that is, moved by the inward taste of the heavenly gifts, by the grace and effects of the sacraments of the Church, by the foretaste of the joys of heaven, and by the abundance of the gifts of the Holy Ghost. These are ointments most sweet and excellent; and that we may be able to reach them, we must follow first of all in the footsteps of the holy humility, patience, meekness and passion of Christ; and through true contrition fall down with the most blessed Magdalen at the feet of the heavenly Bridegroom, and wash them abundantly with tears of penance and kiss them[[Luke 7:38||]]; and then, through worthy satisfaction, spiritual progress and constant guard of the heart, rise to the kisses of his hands; and so, in due order, through the flaming affections of pure and fervent charity and through sincere contemplations of the unchangeable Truth, draw near with the greatest reverence to the kiss of his most pure mouth: and not, like the most wicked traitor[[Matt 26:49||]], thrust ourselves forward with a defiled mind to kiss the mouth of the supreme Holiness.

1.t: Quidam præinducta exponit de Synagoga, quantum ad exitum ejus de terra Ægypti. Quod non videtur congruere : quoniam Sancti veteris Testamenti, nec principaliter nec finaliter optaverunt liberationem illam ab Ægyptiaca servitute ; sed redemptionem a jugo peccati, a servitute diaboli, a reatu culpæ originalis, a spoliatione gloriæ æternalis : cujus redemptionis figura fuit liberatio ex Ægypto.
1.en: A certain writer expounds the foregoing of the Synagogue, as to its going out of the land of Egypt. This does not seem to fit: for the Saints of the Old Testament did not desire, either chiefly or as their end, that deliverance from bondage in Egypt, but redemption from the yoke of sin, from the bondage of the devil, from the guilt of original sin, and from the loss of eternal glory; of which redemption the deliverance from Egypt was a figure.

1.t: Sequitur vox Ecclesiæ ad adolescentulas. Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua : id est, per lucem et gratiam contemplationis erexit me ad incerta et occulta sapientiæ suæ intelligenda, in mysticos intellectus, ad theorias sublimes, ad intuenda abdita Scripturarum, ad speculandum consilium superbeatissimæ Trinitatis de modo salvationis generis humani, per incarnationem et passionem Verbi æterni. Deditque mihi fidem formatam cum rationibus credendorum et purificatæ mentis intelligentia, ut queam ea quæ fidei sunt, evangelizare, persuadere, declarare, defendere. Sicque introduxit me in sanctuarium suum, in amplitudinem divinarum illuminationum ; et per eminentem gradum doni sapientiæ, fecit me quasi secretariam et consiliariam suam rex meus et Deus meus. Insuper, Introduxit me in cellaria sua, ad contemplandas mansiones cœlestes ac gaudia civium supernorum, ut sciam non solum per fidem, sed etiam per prælibationem suavem, per experientiam certam, per revelationem supernaturalem, quæ sit spes vocationis nostræ, ita ut voce filiorum meorum pronuntiem : Nos autem revelata facie gloriam Domini contemplantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur a claritate in claritatem. Nonne in ista cellaria fuit perductus Paulus usque in tertium cœlum raptus, ubi audivit verba arcana, quæ non licet homini loqui?
1.en: There follows the voice of the Church to the young maidens. [[1:3|The king hath brought me into his storerooms|Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua]]: that is, by the light and grace of contemplation he has raised me up to understand [[Ps 50:8|the uncertain and hidden things|incerta et occulta]] of his wisdom [the margin gives Ps. i, 8; the words are from Ps 50:8], to mystical understandings, to sublime contemplations [Latin *theorias*, the Greek word for contemplation], to look into the hidden things of the Scriptures, to behold the counsel of the most blessed Trinity on the manner of the salvation of mankind through the incarnation and passion of the eternal Word. And he has given me formed faith [that is, faith given its life and form by charity], with the reasons for what is to be believed and the understanding of a purified mind, so that I can preach, commend, explain and defend the things of faith. And so my King and my God has brought me into his sanctuary, into the breadth of divine illuminations; and through the eminent degree of the gift of wisdom has made me, as it were, his secretary and counsellor. Moreover, he [[1:3|hath brought me into his storerooms|Introduxit me in cellaria sua]] to contemplate the heavenly mansions and the joys of the citizens above, so that I may know, not by faith alone but also by a sweet foretaste, by sure experience and by supernatural revelation, [[Eph 1:18|what the hope is|quæ sit spes]] of our calling; so that with the voice of my sons I may declare: But we, [[2 Cor 3:18|beholding the glory of the Lord with open face, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory|revelata facie gloriam Domini contemplantes, in eamdem imaginem transformamur a claritate in claritatem]]. Was it not into these storerooms that Paul was brought, [[2 Cor 12:2|caught up to the third heaven|usque in tertium cœlum raptus]], where he [[2 Cor 12:4|heard secret words which it is not granted to man to utter|audivit verba arcana, quæ non licet homini loqui?]]?

1.t: Exsultabimus et lætabimur in te : id est, in contemplatione divitiarum gloriæ tuæ immensæ, et in amore bonitatis tuæ penitus infinitæ, tam vehementer lætabitur cor nostrum, non solum in patria, sed item in via, quod jucunditas ista redundabit in corpus : juxta illud Psalmi, Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum. In spe quoque et prælibatione ac arrha felicitatis futuræ jam gloriamur, dicente Apostolo : Gloriamur in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei; et rursus : Scimus quoniam si terrena domus nostra habitationis hujus dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis. Etenim si in infimis istis sensibilibus rebus videtur alicui gloriandum, nonne incomparabiliter potius videtur gloriandum in superditissimo et superpulcherrimo fonte totius boni? in quo est omnium bonorum desiderabilium et pulcherrimorum plena et infinita possessio, in quo solo tota nostra salus consistit, de quo prædulci et decoro versiculo cantat Propheta : In Deo salutare meum, et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Deo est. Lætabimur ergo in te, o sponse inclyte et decore, memores uberum tuorum, id est beneficiorum gratiæ tuæ, documentorum et præceptorum ac consiliorum tuorum, de quibus jam plenius dictum est, quibus nos alis, super vinum.
1.en: [[1:3|we will be glad and rejoice in thee|Exsultabimus et lætabimur in te]]: that is, in the contemplation of the riches of thy boundless glory and in the love of thy wholly infinite goodness our heart will rejoice so vehemently, not only in our homeland but also on the way, that this gladness will overflow into the body; according to that word of the Psalm: [[Ps 83:3|My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God|Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum]]. In the hope too, and the foretaste and pledge of the happiness to come, we glory already, as the Apostle says: We [[Rom 5:2|glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God|Gloriamur in spe gloriæ filiorum Dei]]; and again: [[2 Cor 5:1|we know, if our earthly house of this habitation be dissolved, that we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in heaven|Scimus quoniam si terrena domus nostra habitationis hujus dissolvatur, quod ædificationem habemus ex Deo, domum non manufactam, æternam in cœlis]]. For if anyone thinks there is glorying to be had in these lowest things of sense, is there not incomparably more to glory in the more than richest and more than most beautiful fountain of all good, in which is the full and infinite possession of all good things desirable and most beautiful, in which alone all our salvation stands; of which the Prophet sings in a most sweet and comely verse: [[Ps 61:8|In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.|In Deo salutare meum, et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Deo est]] We [[1:3|rejoice in thee|lætabimur in te]], then, O glorious and comely Bridegroom, [[1:3|remembering thy breasts|memores uberum tuorum]], that is, the benefits of thy grace, thy teachings, precepts and counsels, of which enough has been said already, with which thou dost nourish us, [[1:3|more than wine|super vinum]].

1.t: Recti diligunt te, non solum amore naturali et acquisito, sed potius amore gratuito, supernaturali, infuso. Quum enim sis ipsa bonitatis essentia, bonitas pura et infinita, in infinitum pulchrior, dulcior, convenientior, amabilior universis ac singulis, a quo quidquid bonum et amabile est, omnem suam bonitatem ac amabilitatem sortitum est; quicumque non diligit te, sicut tu ipse jussisti, toto corde, omnino curvus, perversus, ingratus, insipiensque esse convincitur. Recti itaque, id est justi, qui exhibent unicuique quod ei tenentur, te diligunt: quoniam exhibent tibi se ipsos, et amori tuo ac cultui mancipant jam se totos, ad quod non solum ex tua bonitate, sed et ex beneficiis tuis quæ susceperunt, tenentur; et quia tu prior amasti eos, et præparasti eis te ipsum in præmium.
1.en: [[1:3|the rightous love thee|Recti diligunt te]], not only with natural and acquired love, but rather with a love freely given, supernatural and infused. For since thou art the very essence of goodness, pure and infinite goodness, infinitely more beautiful, sweeter, more fitting and more lovable than all things together and each one, from whom whatever is good and lovable has received all its goodness and lovableness, whoever does not love thee as thou thyself hast commanded, [[Matt 22:37|with thy whole heart|toto corde]], is proved to be altogether crooked, perverse, ungrateful and foolish. [[1:3|The rightous|Recti]], then, that is, the just, who render to each what they owe him, [[1:3|love thee|te diligunt]]: for they render themselves to thee, and now give themselves wholly over to thy love and worship, to which they are bound not only by thy goodness but also by the benefits they have received from thee; and because thou didst first love them[[1 John 4:10||]][[1 John 4:19||]], and hast prepared thyself for them as their reward[[John 14:3||]].

1.t: Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem. Ecclesia nigram se nominat : Primo, quoniam multi imperfecti, fragiles et infirmi ac peccatores in ea sunt : propter quod Christus comparat eam sagenæ missæ in mare, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti. Secundo, quia et ipsi electi ac boni, quotidie et frequenter in venialibus peccant, et eorum justitiæ quasi pannus menstruatæ censentur. Tertio, quia in vita hac variis tribulationibus, tentationibus, adversitatibus exercentur. Verumtamen ipsa se formosam fatetur, quoniam semper multi virtuosi et sancti in ea consistunt, et omnes qui ei vere incorporantur, caritate virtutibusque infusis ac donis Spiritus Sancti ornantur. Habet etiam sacramenta, quibus quotidie renovatur ac pulchrificatur. Itaque, Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem, id est, animæ, seu adolescentulæ ac particulares Ecclesiæ, sicut tabernacula Cedar : qui fuit secundus filius Ismaelis, et habitavit ipse Cedar cum sobole sua atque familia in tabernaculis et in solitudine, seu deserto; sicque tabernacula ejus foris quandoque deformia, utpote ventis imbribusque exposita, intus erant divitiis et pecoribus plena; sicut pelles Salomonis : quibus ipse domum suam thalamumve ornavit, aut tabernaculum Dei seu vasa ejus operuit. Melius tamen per Salomonem intelligitur Christus: cujus pelles sunt speciosi vestitus ministrorum suorum, et ornamenta cultus divini, mores quoque et exteriores gestus, incessus et apparatus ipsius Christi, quibus se ejus sponsa conformat pro posse. His etenim tanquam optimis pellibus vestitur ac decoratur Ecclesia. Denique, per tabernacula Cedar possunt intelligi perfidi et gentiles, quibus infidelis Judæa similem reputavit Ecclesiam, contemnens eamdem.
1.en: [[1:4|I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem]]. The Church calls herself black: first, because there are in her many who are imperfect, frail and weak, and sinners; for which reason Christ compares her to [[Matt 13:47|a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kinds of fishes|sagenæ missæ in mare, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti]]. Secondly, because even the elect and the good sin daily and often in venial sins, and their justices are reckoned [[Is 64:6|as the rag of a menstruous woman|quasi pannus menstruatæ]]. Thirdly, because in this life they are tried by various tribulations, temptations and adversities. Yet she owns herself beautiful, because there are always many virtuous and holy men in her, and all who are truly made members of her are adorned with charity, infused virtues and the gifts of the Holy Ghost. She has the sacraments too, by which she is daily renewed and made beautiful. So: [[1:4|I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, souls, or young maidens and particular Churches, [[1:4|as the tents of Cedar|sicut tabernacula Cedar]]: Cedar was the second son of Ismael[[Gen 25:13||]], and lived with his offspring and household in tents, in the wilderness or desert; and so his tents, though at times unsightly without, being exposed to winds and rains, were within full of riches and cattle. [[1:4|as the curtains of Solomon|sicut pelles Salomonis]] [Latin *pelles*, skins or hides, where the Douay-Rheims has "curtains"]: with which he adorned his house or bridal chamber, or covered the tabernacle of God or its vessels. But Solomon is better understood as Christ, whose skins are the fair garments of his ministers and the ornaments of divine worship, and also the manners and outward bearing, the gait and attire of Christ himself, to which his Bride conforms herself as far as she can. For with these, as with the finest skins, the Church is clothed and adorned. Lastly, by the tents of Cedar may be understood the faithless and the heathen, to whom unbelieving Judea, despising the Church, reckoned her alike.

1.t: Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim, id est obscura seu denigrata, juxta sensum quo dixi, Nigra sum; quia decoloravit me sol, id est, comparatione sanctitatis, perfectionis ac sapientiæ sponsi mei, qui est Sol sapientiæ atque justitiæ, fuscam me fateor: qui etiam legem tantæ perfectionis contulit mihi, quod a perfecta ejus observatione deficio; sicque legis suæ splendore me fuscam demonstrat. Rursus, Decoloravit me sol, id est, intuitu et amore solis istius, videlicet sponsi, exposui me tribulationibus, persecutionibus ac aspernationibus impiorum, laboribusque diversis ac multis doloribus: propter quos videor decolorata, et quasi relicta a sponso. Sed hæc omnia intus me ornant: idcirco nolite ista in me ita considerare, ut metu sustinendi talia, recedatis a fide et obedientia mea; sed præmia illa æterna pro his momentaneis afflictionibus exhibenda, perpendite, et gaudete in talibus, sicut in Evangelio sponsus hortatur: Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Postremo, per solem hoc loco quidam æstum tribulationis intelligunt.
1.en: [[1:5|Do not consider me that I am brown|Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim]], that is, dark or blackened, in the sense in which I said, [[1:4|I am black|Nigra sum]]; [[1:5|because the sun hath altered my colour|quia decoloravit me sol]]: that is, I confess myself brown in comparison with the holiness, perfection and wisdom of my Bridegroom, who is the Sun of wisdom and justice; who has also given me a law of such perfection that I fall short of keeping it perfectly; and so by the splendour of his law he shows me to be brown. Again, [[1:5|the sun hath altered my colour|decoloravit me sol]]: that is, for the sake of beholding and loving this Sun, namely the Bridegroom, I have exposed myself to tribulations, persecutions and the contempt of the wicked, to labours of many kinds and many sorrows; because of which I seem discoloured, and as it were forsaken by the Bridegroom. But all these adorn me within; therefore do not so consider these things in me that for fear of suffering the like you draw back from my faith and obedience; but weigh those eternal rewards that are to be given for these momentary afflictions, and rejoice in such things, as the Bridegroom exhorts in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:12|Be glad|Gaudete]] in that hour [[Matt 5:12|and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]] [Denis's "in that hour" is closer to Luke 6:23, "in that day"]. Lastly, some take the sun in this place for the heat of tribulation.

1.t: Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me. Ecclesia primitiva ex Judæis atque gentilibus fuit collecta, sicque mater Ecclesiæ partim fuit ipsa gentilitas, partim plebs Judæorum. Ipsam autem Ecclesiam primitivam multis annis acerrime impugnaverunt tam infideles ac obstinati Judæi, quam gentiles increduli, prout in Actibus Apostolorum partim describitur, atque in chronicis, historiis et legendis Sanctorum plenius continetur.
