Judæi autem impugnaverunt eam tam allegationibus Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, quam persecutione reali. Similiter gentiles philosophi, ratione naturali variis modis contra Ecclesiam dimicarunt; reges vero et tyranni fecerunt hoc gladio materiali. Et sicut sponsus prædixit, tradebantur credentes in eum a parentibus, fratribus, cognatis et amicis, et morte afficiebantur ab eis. — Insuper universalis Ecclesia in persona particularium Ecclesiarum, hoc est quæcumque particularis Ecclesia, dicere potest: Filii matris meæ, hoc est hæretici qui ad tempus fuerunt universalis Ecclesiæ filii (de quibus in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes apostolus, Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis), pugnaverunt contra me, quia valde fuerunt infesti Catholicis, potissime Ariani: qui et corporaliter pluribus annis persequebantur et jugulabant fideles. Similiter impii Christiani, schismatici, principesque iniqui et vitiosi prælati pugnant adversus Ecclesiam, justos vexando, pusillos ac subditos scandalizando, injusta prælia suscitando, aut ecclesiasticis non obediendo mandatis. Et certe pia mater Ecclesia, quæ a malignis spiritibus et ab infidelibus populis incessanter gravissime impugnatur, non mediocriter contristatur, dum filios suos, qui se deberent mutuo contra prætactos hostes acerrimos adjuvare, videt contra se matrem ipsorum et contra se invicem decertare.
1.en: [[1:5|the sons of my mother have fought against me|Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me]]. The early Church was gathered from Jews and Gentiles, and so the mother of the Church was partly the Gentile world itself and partly the Jewish people. And this early Church was most fiercely assailed for many years both by the unbelieving and obstinate Jews and by the unbelieving Gentiles, as is described in part in the Acts of the Apostles and is set out more fully in the chronicles, histories and legends of the Saints. The Jews assailed her both by citing the Scriptures of the Old Testament and by actual persecution. So too the Gentile philosophers fought against the Church in various ways by natural reason; while kings and tyrants did so with the material sword. And as the Bridegroom foretold, those who believed in him were betrayed by parents, brethren, kinsmen and friends, and were put to death by them [see Luke 21:16]. Moreover, the universal Church in the person of the particular Churches, that is, any particular Church, can say: [[1:5|the sons of my mother|Filii matris meæ]], that is, the heretics who for a time were sons of the universal Church (of whom the apostle John says in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us|Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis]]), [[1:5|have fought against me|pugnaverunt contra me]], because they were very hostile to Catholics, above all the Arians, who also for many years persecuted and slaughtered the faithful in body. So too wicked Christians, schismatics, unjust princes and vicious prelates fight against the Church, by harassing the just, by scandalizing the little ones and their subjects, by stirring up unjust wars, or by not obeying the commands of the Church. And truly our loving mother the Church, who is ceaselessly and most grievously assailed by evil spirits and by unbelieving peoples, is not a little saddened when she sees her sons, who ought to help one another against those fiercest enemies just named, fighting against their own mother and against one another.

1.t: Posuerunt me custodem in vineis : id est, infideles Judæi me in terra sua persequendo, atque ex ea me repellendo, fuerunt occasio, quod cœpi per totam gentilitatem dispergi, atque gentilibus toto orbe terrarum evangelizare: in quibus innumerabilia millia paganorum converti, et multas fundavi particulares Ecclesias, tanquam vineas Dei, quas pastorali sollicitudine custodivi, excolui, fecundavi. Hinc in apostolicis Actis Paulus et Barnabas obduratis loquuntur Judæis: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes: sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus, Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ. Vineam meam non custodivi : id est, Synagogam mihi commissam juste reliqui : et hoc, propter obstinationem, rebellionem, et incorrigibilitatem ipsius. Primitivæ namque Ecclesiæ, id est Apostolis et eorum adjutoribus, jussit Christus primo prædicare Judæis. Nam ante passionem suam præcepit : In viam gentium ne abieritis; sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel. Post resurrectionem vero præcepit eisdem Apostolis : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Nihilo minus intentio Christi fuit, ut adhuc primo ad tempus prædicarent Judæis : quod et pene per tredecim annos fecerunt pro majori parte ipsi gloriosi Apostoli, quousque divisi sunt. Interim tamen a tempore persecutionis factæ sub Stephano, sub qua (præter Apostolos) omnes discipuli fuerunt dispersi, coeperunt per totam Galilæam atque Samariam prædicare, sicut et Paulus ac Barnabas alibi : attamen Judæis dumtaxat, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum manifeste habetur. Tandem Judæis undique obduratis, ad gentilium conversionem profecti sunt.
1.en: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews, by persecuting me in their land and driving me out of it, were the occasion of my beginning to be scattered through the whole Gentile world and to preach the Gospel to the Gentiles throughout the world; among whom I converted countless thousands of pagans and founded many particular Churches, as vineyards of God, which I kept, tilled and made fruitful with pastoral care. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles Paul and Barnabas say to the hardened Jews: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes]]: [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus]], [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ]] [the margin gives both Acts 13:46–47 and Is. xlix, 6, which the Apostles are quoting; Denis's "my salvation" follows Isaias]. [[1:5|my vineyard I have not kept|Vineam meam non custodivi]]: that is, I justly left the Synagogue entrusted to me, and this because of its obstinacy, rebellion and incorrigibility. For Christ commanded the early Church, that is, the Apostles and their helpers, to preach first to the Jews. For before his passion he commanded: [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]]; [[Matt 10:6|But go ye rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel|sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel]]. But after the resurrection he commanded the same Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. Nevertheless it was Christ's intention that they should still preach first to the Jews for a time; and this the glorious Apostles themselves did for the most part for nearly thirteen years, until they were separated. In the meantime, however, from the time of the persecution raised under Stephen, in which all the disciples except the Apostles were scattered[[Acts 8:1||]], they began to preach through all Galilee and Samaria, as did Paul and Barnabas elsewhere, yet to the Jews only, as is plainly found in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 13:46||]]. At last, when the Jews were hardened everywhere, they set out to convert the Gentiles.

1.t: Insuper Ecclesia ex persona carnalium ac negligentium prælatorum dicere potest : Posuerunt me custodem in vineis: id est, Christus et ejus Apostoli præceperunt mihi, cum omni diligentia præsidere ac providere particularibus Ecclesiis Dei. Sic namque princeps Apostolorum hortatur : Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei. Et Paulus : Qui præest, in sollicitudine, supple, præsit. Vineam meam, id est vineas mihi commissas, non custodivi : per singulare intelligendo plurale, ut moris est in Scripturis.
1.en: Moreover, the Church can say in the person of carnal and negligent prelates: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, Christ and his Apostles commanded me to preside over and provide for the particular Churches of God with all diligence. For so the prince of the Apostles exhorts: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei]]. And Paul: [[Rom 12:8|he that ruleth, with carefulness|Qui præest, in sollicitudine]], supply: let him rule. [[1:5|my vineyard|Vineam meam]], that is, the vineyards entrusted to me, [[1:5|I have not kept|non custodivi]]: understanding the plural by the singular, as is the custom in the Scriptures.

1.t: Circa hæc ait Anselmus : Quemadmodum vineæ quatuor modis læduntur præcipue, sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ totidem adversa, maxime in suis membris teneris, solent nocere. Vineæ etenim obest asperum frigus, et urens ventus, spissaque grando, et nimia pluvia. Sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ in suis membris aliquando nocet frigus seu torpor exemplorum malorum: quoniam sicut frigus seu gelu stringit atque exterminat vineæ florem, sic malum exemplum aufert a tenero corde conceptæ devotionis amorem. Aliquando etiam ei obest ventus diabolicæ suggestionis, adurens renes mentis et corporis. Nocere etiam maxime solet grando pessimæ detractionis et dissensionis, quæ dissipat florem fraternæ dilectionis. Pluvia quoque pravæ doctrinæ, et prosperitatis assiduæ, solet plerumque statum mentis dissolvere, et ad amorem mundi reflectere. Sicut e contrario prodest vineæ suavis aura cum dulci rore, sic prodest Ecclesiæ pax cum salubri sermone. Præterea, sicut vinitores non custodiunt vineas, qui eas non putant, non considerant, non excolunt, nec fructum ex eis colligere conantur; ita prælati qui sibi commissis pravos mores, inordinata colloquia, opera illicita non præcidunt, nec qualiter subditi circa divinorum observantiam præceptorum se habeant, intuentur; nec corripiendo, corrigendo, exhortando, docendo, obsecrando, comminando, et orando pro eis, reformare eos conantur, neque exemplis neque verbis satagunt fructum virtutum et spiritualem assiduumque profectum ex ipsis producere, nequaquam ut tenentur vineas Dei commissas sibi custodiunt. Ideo sanguinem pereuntium Dominus requiret ab eis.
1.en: On these words Anselm says: As vineyards are harmed chiefly in four ways, so the same number of adversities are wont to harm holy Church, above all in her tender members. For a vineyard is harmed by bitter cold, scorching wind, thick hail and too much rain. So holy Church is sometimes harmed in her members by the cold or numbness of bad examples: for as cold or frost nips and destroys the flower of the vine, so a bad example takes from a tender heart the love of the devotion it had conceived. Sometimes too she is harmed by the wind of the devil's suggestion, scorching the reins of mind and body. The hail of most wicked detraction and dissension is also wont to do the greatest harm, for it scatters the flower of brotherly love. The rain too of false doctrine and of constant prosperity often loosens the state of the mind and turns it back to the love of the world. As, on the contrary, a gentle breeze with sweet dew does good to the vineyard, so peace with wholesome preaching does good to the Church. Further, as vinedressers do not keep their vineyards who do not prune them, do not look to them, do not till them, and do not try to gather fruit from them; so prelates who do not cut away the evil manners, disorderly talk and unlawful works of those entrusted to them, nor look to how their subjects stand in keeping God's commandments, nor try to reform them by rebuking, correcting, exhorting, teaching, beseeching, threatening and praying for them, nor take pains by example or by word to bring forth from them the fruit of virtues and steady spiritual progress, by no means keep the vineyards of God entrusted to them as they are bound to. Therefore the Lord will require the blood of those who perish at their hands[[Ezech 33:6||]][[Ezech 33:8||]].

1.t: Sed quoniam primitiva Ecclesia a Judæis dispersa, et per gentilitatem divisa, innumerabiles persecutiones sustinuit, sicut et Paulus in suis epistolis de se patefecit, recte subjungit Ecclesia : Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie : id est, tu, sponse cœlestis super omnia prædilecte, mihi dignanter ostende ubi tu gratiose commoreris, in quorum cordibus pabula internæ refectionis exhibeas, quos pastoraliter nutris. Indica etiam mihi ubi cubes, id est, stabiliter requiescas, quorum mentes tibi carissimas luce contemplationis perfundas : ita quod per contemplativæ exercitia vitæ, te intra se jugiter complectuntur, retinent, nec offendunt, ita ut illud Deuteronomii impleatur in eis : Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet.
1.en: But since the early Church, scattered by the Jews and spread through the Gentile world, endured countless persecutions, as Paul too makes known of himself in his epistles[[2 Cor 11:23||]] [the margin gives II Cor. xi, 23–27], the Church rightly adds: [[1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]]: that is, thou, heavenly Bridegroom, beloved above all things, graciously show me where thou dost dwell in thy grace, in whose hearts thou dost set the food of inward refreshment, whom thou dost feed as a shepherd. [[1:6|Shew me|Indica mihi]] also [[1:6|where thou liest|ubi cubes]], that is, where thou dost steadfastly rest: whose minds, most dear to thee, thou dost flood with the light of contemplation, so that through the exercises of the contemplative life they hold thee constantly embraced within them, keep thee, and do not offend thee; so that that word of Deuteronomy is fulfilled in them: [[Deut 33:12|The best beloved of the Lord shall dwell confidently in him: as in a bride chamber shall he abide all the day long, and between his shoulders shall be rest|Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet]].
